decisions.reason: After several years this adjustable quarter-pallet display has likely shown enough market acceptance, and because it remains close to the cardboard core offer it is still inexpensive and strategically sensible to retain.
The pegboard-back display fits the firm's established design and production capabilities and, if still offered by 2022, likely has sufficient customer traction to justify keeping it in the portfolio.

By 2022 the uncertainty around this more standard quarter-pallet concept should be largely resolved, and its overlap with other cardboard display options makes it a comparatively weak option to continue carrying.

The wooden display pallet sits farther from the firm's paper-based core and is likely costlier to support, so once several years of learning have passed management would be inclined to release resources back to core displays and new development.
